## Project

The Accountability Project is an effort to cut across data silos and give
journalists, policy professionals, activists, and the public at large a simple
way to search across huge volumes of public data about people and organizations.

Our goal is to standardizing public data on a few key fields by thinking of each
dataset row as a transaction. For each transaction there should be (at least) 3
variables:

1. All **parties** to a transaction.
2. The **date** of the transaction.
3. The **amount** of money involved.

## Objectives

This document describes the process used to complete the following objectives:

1. How many records are in the database?
1. Check for entirely duplicated records.
1. Check ranges of continuous variables.
1. Is there anything blank or missing?
1. Check for consistency issues.
1. Create a five-digit ZIP Code called `zip`.
1. Create a `year` field from the transaction date.
1. Make sure there is data on both parties to a transaction.

## Packages

The following packages are needed to collect, manipulate, visualize, analyze,
and communicate these results. The `pacman` package will facilitate their
installation and attachment.

The IRW's `campfin` package will also have to be installed from GitHub. This
package contains functions custom made to help facilitate the processing of
campaign finance data.

```{r load_packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE}
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load_gh("irworkshop/campfin")
pacman::p_load(
  tidyverse, # data manipulation
  lubridate, # datetime strings
  magrittr, # pipe operators
  jsonlite, # parse json files
  janitor, # data frame clean
  aws.s3, # read from aws s3
  refinr, # cluster and merge
  scales, # format strings
  knitr, # knit documents
  vroom, # read files fast
  glue, # combine strings
  here, # relative storage
  fs # search storage 
)
```

This document should be run as part of the `R_campfin` project, which lives as a
sub-directory of the more general, language-agnostic
[`irworkshop/accountability_datacleaning`][tap] GitHub repository.

The `R_campfin` project uses the [RStudio projects][rproj] feature and should be
run as such. The project also uses the dynamic `here::here()` tool for file
paths relative to _your_ machine.

## Data

The contracts [data] is from the Washington state [Department of Enterprise 
Services][des]. The data can be retrieved from the Washington OpenData portal
under the title "Master Contract Sales Data by Customer, Contract, Vendor" in
the "Procurement and Contracts" category. The data file was last updated on
January 21, 2020. As of writing, due to the ongoing Covid-19 pandemic, our
typical efforts to verify this OpenData source as the most updated were not 
made. 

[data]: https://data.wa.gov/Procurements-and-Contracts/Master-Contract-Sales-Data-by-Customer-Contract-Ve/n8q6-4twj
[des]: https://des.wa.gov/

## Import

We can import the text file directly into R from the OpenData portal URL.

```{r raw_read}
wac <- vroom(
  file = "https://data.wa.gov/api/views/n8q6-4twj/rows.csv",
  .name_repair = make_clean_names,
  col_types = cols(
    `Calendar Year` = col_integer(),
    `Q1 Sales Reported` = col_double(),
    `Q2 Sales Reported` = col_double(),
    `Q3 Sales Reported` = col_double(),
    `Q4 Sales Reported` = col_double(),
  )
)
```

Then we can convert some quasi-logical variables to a true logical type.

```{r raw_convert}
count(wac, vet_owned)
wac <- mutate_at(
  .tbl = wac,
  .vars = vars(12:14),
  .funs = equals, "Y"
)
```

## Explore

```{r glimpse}
glimpse(wac)
tail(wac)
```

### Missing

```{r na_count}
col_stats(wac, count_na)
```

About 6% of transactions are missing the customer name.

```{r na_flag}
wac <- wac %>% flag_na(customer_name, vendor_name)
percent(mean(wac$na_flag), 0.01)
```

### Duplicates

There are also a small handful of duplicate records, all also missing a name.

```{r dupe_flag}
wac <- flag_dupes(wac, everything())
sum(wac$dupe_flag)
```

```{r dupe_view}
wac %>% 
  filter(dupe_flag) %>% 
  select(customer_name, vendor_name, calendar_year)
```

### Categorical

```{r distinct_each}
col_stats(wac, n_distinct)
```

```{r distinct_count}
wac %>% 
  select(12:15) %>% 
  map(~mutate(count(data.frame(x = .x), x), p = n/sum(n)))
```

### Amounts

The amount paid to each vendor for a contract is broken up into fiscal quarters.
We will sum the quarters to find the total annual spending.

```{r amouunt_sum}
wac <- wac %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(amount = sum(c_across(ends_with("sales_reported"))))
```

```{r ammount_summary}
summary(wac$amount)
percent(mean(wac$amount <= 0), 0.01)
```

```{r hist_amount, echo=FALSE}
wac %>%
  ggplot(aes(amount)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = dark2["purple"]) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1 %o% 10^(0:6)),
    labels = dollar,
    trans = "log10"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Washington Contracts Amount Distribution",
    subtitle = "from 2000 to 2019",
    caption = "Source: WA DES",
    x = "Amount",
    y = "Count"
  )
```

### Dates

The data goes back to `r min(wac$calendar_year)` and the number of contracts is
extremely consistent year to year.

```{r bar_year, echo=FALSE}
wac %>% 
  count(calendar_year) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = calendar_year, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = dark2["orange"]) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_x_continuous() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(
    title = "Washington Contracts by Year",
    caption = "Source: WA DES",
    fill = "Election Year",
    x = "Year Made",
    y = "Count"
  )
```

## Conclude

```{r clean_glimpse}
glimpse(wac)
```

1. There are `r comma(nrow(wac))` records in the database.
1. There are `r comma(sum(wac$dupe_flag))` duplicate records in the database.
1. The range and distribution of `amount` and `date` seem reasonable.
1. There are `r comma(sum(wac$na_flag))` records missing a name.
1. There is no geographic data to normalize.
1. The 4-digit `calendar_year` variable already exists.

## Update

```{r old_read}
wac_old <- s3read_using(
  FUN = read_csv,
  object = "csv/wa_contracts.csv",
  bucket = "publicaccountability"
)

wac_old$omwbe[is.na(wac_old$omwbe)] <- "N"
```

```{r old_new}
wac_new <- wac %>% 
  filter(calendar_year > 2020)
```

```{r old_2020}
wac_old_2020 <- wac_old %>% 
  filter(calendar_year == 2020)

wac_new_2020 <- wac %>% 
  filter(calendar_year == 2020)
```

```{r old_combine}
wac_new <- bind_rows(wac_new, wac_new_2020)
```

## Export

Now the file can be saved on disk for upload to the Accountability server. We
will name the object using a date range of the records included.

```{r clean-dir}
clean_dir <- dir_create(here("state", "wa", "contracts", "data", "clean"))
clean_csv <- path(clean_dir, "wa_contracts_2015-20221129.csv")
clean_rds <- path_ext_set(clean_csv, "rds")
basename(clean_csv)
```

```{r clean-write}
write_csv(wac, clean_csv, na = "")
write_rds(wac, clean_rds, compress = "xz")
(clean_size <- file_size(clean_csv))
```

## Upload

We can use the `aws.s3::put_object()` to upload the text file to the IRW server.

```{r aws-upload, eval=FALSE}
aws_key <- path("csv", basename(clean_csv))
if (!object_exists(aws_key, "publicaccountability")) {
  put_object(
    file = clean_csv,
    object = aws_key, 
    bucket = "publicaccountability",
    acl = "public-read",
    show_progress = TRUE,
    multipart = TRUE
  )
}
aws_head <- head_object(aws_key, "publicaccountability")
(aws_size <- as_fs_bytes(attr(aws_head, "content-length")))
unname(aws_size == clean_size)
```

## Update: October 2026

_Rebuilt 2026-10-14 for The Accountability Project (Claude, for Jacob Fenton); published 2026-10-15. The runnable
script is [`code/wa_contracts.R`](../code/wa_contracts.R); the steps above are unchanged except as noted here.
Output: `wa_contracts_2015-2026.csv`, 245,831 rows, the same 17 columns in the same order._

The source is the same Washington OpenData export ([`n8q6-4twj`][data], now titled "Statewide Contract (Master
Contract) Sales Data by Customer, Contract, Vendor"), downloaded 2026-10-14 (portal updated 2026-04-24): 245,831 rows,
14 columns, calendar years 2015-2026 (2026 is partial). It is the full history, so this is a **full replacement** of
`wa_contracts.csv` (172,773 rows, 2015 to part of 2022), not an append. Changes:

1. **No "Update" step.** The 2022 step above (keep 2021 onward, re-take 2020, then bind) is not needed.
2. **Read** from the downloaded file rather than the URL; the column types are set on the cleaned names.
3. Columns 12-14 (`vet_owned`, `small_business`, `diverse_options`) become logical with `across()`, since
   `mutate_at(..., equals, "Y")` needs magrittr; a blank `omwbe` becomes `"N"`, as before.
4. `amount` is the sum of the four quarterly sales (no quarter is blank).
5. **Amendments.** The source has no amendment or superseded flag; nothing is dropped.

`na_flag` (blank customer name) marks 12,315 rows and `dupe_flag` 8. For 2015-2021 the rows and amounts per year are
within 0.2% of the old file, and rows that match on customer, contract, vendor and year have identical amounts. 2022
grows from 18,602 to 20,478 rows (the old file had only part of 2022); new years: 2023 20,545 rows ($2.77 billion),
2024 21,699 ($3.31 billion), 2025 21,439 ($3.24 billion), 2026 7,525 so far ($0.40 billion).

**The state now shows current names on past years.** About 3,900 old rows (2015-2021) no longer match by key, nearly
all because the export shows the vendor's or customer's *current* name: 2,840 vendor renames (for example BUD CLARY
AUTO DEALERSHIPS is now BUD CLARY CHEVROLET INC on 964 rows, and MAGNA5, LLC is RINGSQUARED TELECOM LLC on 327) and
858 customer-name fixes (GR HARBOR COLLEGE is GRAYS HARBOR COLLEGE). As decided for this update, we use what the state
publishes, so the old names for those years are no longer in the data.

```{r update-2026-read, eval=FALSE}
wac <- read_csv("raw_n8q6-4twj.csv", name_repair = make_clean_names,
                col_types = cols(.default = col_character(), calendar_year = col_integer(),
                                 q1_sales_reported = col_double(), q2_sales_reported = col_double(),
                                 q3_sales_reported = col_double(), q4_sales_reported = col_double()))
wac <- mutate(wac, across(12:14, ~ .x == "Y"))
wac$omwbe[is.na(wac$omwbe)] <- "N"
wac <- flag_na(wac, customer_name, vendor_name)
wac <- flag_dupes(wac, everything())
wac <- mutate(wac, amount = q1_sales_reported + q2_sales_reported + q3_sales_reported + q4_sales_reported)
```
